QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_10

question.text: Can a Non-Profit Organisation ever issue equity on the SSE, and if so, under what condition?

answer.text: No — no NPO can ever issue equity because equity represents a residual claim on profits, and NPOs do not distribute profits.
Yes — any NPO can issue equity provided it surrenders its Section 12A / 12AB registration beforehand.
Yes — only a Section 8 Company can issue equity/debt, because Section 8 allows share organisation, though it prohibits dividend payment.
Yes — Section 8 Companies, Trusts and Societies can all issue equity subject to SEBI approval on a case-by-case basis.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 2.2 and Section 2.3.1.3, among NPO legal forms only Section 8 Companies can organise on a share basis under the Companies Act 2013. However the shares are not residual claims on profits — Section 8 companies cannot pay dividends. Trusts and Societies have no share capital and cannot issue equity. The Section 8 equity listing on SSE requires social performance track record and follows standard listing norms. The Trap: Option A overstates the restriction — Section 8 equity is an exception. Option B invents a 12A surrender route. Option D wrongly extends the ability to Trusts and Societies. Cross-Exam Context: V-B (MF Foundation) and X-A/X-B (IA L1/L2) treat equity fundamentals where 'residual claim on profits' is standard; XXIII inverts this for Section 8. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When auditing a Section 8 company listed on SSE, flag the 'no-dividend' restriction explicitly in your materiality note — investors sometimes assume equity-like returns and the Annual Impact Report should state clearly that the return is social, not financial.
